subject: End-of-Q OKR scoring: consolidated scores, narrative edits, and open decisions
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: End-of-Q OKR scoring: consolidated scores, narrative edits, and open decisions

Team — attaching consolidated EOQ scoring and the narrative deck we’ll take into the exec QBR next week. Key asks: please review the XLSX and the Narrative draft (QBR_narrative_draft_v3.pdf) and reply with any substantive rewording or score objections by EOD Monday PST. I captured a short set of open decisions below.

Attachments: EOQ_OKR_scores_v1.2.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), QBR_narrative_draft_v3.pdf (deck stub)

Top-level summary (TL;DR)
- Overall: We’re recommending a 7/10 on the serving-runtime objective (see notes).
- Two asks from leadership: finalize the evidence lines for the "reliability" KR and approve the risk language on quantization rollouts.

Open decisions (need owners):
1) Reliability evidence: Laura to confirm final artifact list (logs, incident timeline, test harness).
2) Serving runtime score: Marcus suggested re-eval based on production latency distribution; Vivek please weigh in.
3) QBR narrative tone: Should the executive slide call out the paired-customer story (Acme) or keep it anonymized? (Sara and Acme are aware; we can request permission)

Proposed deadlines
- Score/wording freeze: Mon 2027-02-28 17:00 PST
- Final deck to marketing for slide polish: Tue 2027-03-01 11:00 PST

Quick context notes added inline in the spreadsheet — I flagged KRs with weak evidence in red. Please inline comments in the XLSX and add line notes in the PDF if you want language edits.

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Strategy & Planning
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: End-of-Q OKR scoring: consolidated scores, narrative edits, and open decisions

Soojin — thanks for pulling this together. Quick notes:
- I agree with the 7/10 for the serving-runtime objective given production tail latency incidents in Jan; but suggest we move to a 6.5/10 (or mark as 7 with a footnote) because two SLO breaches occurred on the same week.
- On the Acme story: I’m comfortable calling them out by name for QBR if we note their role as an early pilot and include a short anonymized appendix for external audiences. Sara should confirm.

Small edit: in the deck slide 4 (KR breakdown) can we rephrase the "latency regression" line to "latency variance observed in Jan; mitigations deployed" — that reads less like a recurring failure.

Vivek
VP, Product

Adding my lane on evidence: I reviewed the red-flagged KRs and pulled the artifacts we need for the evidence binder. I’ll add the incident timeline (Jan 11 outage), the postmortem summary, and the synthetic test results to the shared Drive in a folder called "EOQ Evidence - reliability" by Monday noon.

A couple of narrative suggestions:
- When we call out the reliability regression, explicitly link the remediation (KV cache fix + kernel change) to the latency improvement; that helps the story of ownership and remediation.
- For the "customer impact" slide, the Acme pilot example could have a one-line quote from Sara if she’s willing. If Sara is not comfortable, I suggest we use the anonymized metric instead (">10% throughput improvement for pilot customer")

I made three small inline comments in the XLSX (cells B12, C13, D18).

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: End-of-Q OKR scoring: consolidated scores, narrative edits, and open decisions

Team — I reviewed the metrics and want to push back on the proposed final score for Serving Runtime. My read: the latency regressions were limited to a specific quantized model rollout, which we rolled back within 48 hours. The steady-state distribution for the month is still within acceptable bounds. I propose we keep 7/10 but add a note in the narrative that this was a targeted rollout incident and list the rollback and fix as mitigation steps.

If leadership wants stricter wording, we should reflect that as a separate risk mitigation KR rather than lowering the objective for the whole objective group.

Marcus
Head of Serving Runtime
